previous_assumption: Quotation, Negotiation, and Award needed their own dedicated cross-module wiring separate from Rental.
correction: CommercialQuotationService.awardQuotation calls RentalService.createRental directly (an application-service-to-application-service call, not a repository-port call) rather than duplicating Rental's machine-ownership/retired/availability validation. This is a deliberate exception to the usual "cross-module reads go through the other module's repository port" convention (e.g. EquipmentService reads catalogue via ProductRepositoryPort) — here the whole point is to reuse Rental's business logic, not just its data, so the other module's *application service* is the crossed boundary instead. Award is always the same action regardless of origin (Path A response, Path B direct, Path C auction win): flip quotation status to "awarded" only after RentalService.createRental succeeds, so a failed award (e.g. a machine double-booked in the meantime) never leaves the quotation in an inconsistent state. Verified end to end: RFQ -> response -> quotation -> negotiated counter-offer -> award correctly produced a Rental at the negotiated (not original) rate, and auto-closed the source Requirement.
